# A Session schema for the agents sidebar

- Status: in progress (the schema, its page and the sidebar's rows are built; the sessions table is left)
- Links: [research](../../docs/research/0001-agent-session.md) · PR #18 (the agents sidebar) · PR #20 (Session in the glossary) · [icebox: the sign-in session table](0002-auth-session-name.md) · PR #28 · [ADR 0010](../../docs/adr/0010-a-session-keeps-what-most-sources-keep.md)

The agents sidebar kept each row's `state`, task kind, title and nesting in the web app alone: `AgentState` and `AgentTask` were the keys of `stateIcons` and `taskIcons` in `web/next/src/components/agents/icons.ts`, and `title` and `subagents` sat on the row types in `agents/sidebar.tsx`. All four describe one run of an agent, which the glossary calls a Session, so they moved into a `Session` schema in `packages/schema`, beside `Agent`. A subagent's run becomes a child session that points at the session that started it, as OpenCode, Codex and eve model it.

## Decided

1. **The field's name is `status`** (2026-10-20), the name seven of the nine sources use, so the icons page's State section becomes Status.
2. **All nine values stay** (2026-10-20, sorted A to Z 2026-10-21): cancelled, completed, failed, idle, paused, pending, running, stuck and waiting. Sessions run as CLIs in herdr panes, where a rate limit pauses a session and an unrecognized screen can leave it stuck, so each value has a way to be detected: herdr's own status (`working`, `blocked`, `idle`), the harness's hooks (a `StopFailure` with `rate_limit`) and its wording on screen, or the server (a session that stopped making progress).
3. **Stuck and waiting stay apart** (2026-10-20). Waiting: the agent asked the human something on purpose, a question or a permission, which the UI can answer. Stuck: the agent is not moving and asked nothing the server understands, such as an unrecognized screen or one that has not changed for a long time, so a person has to look at the pane.
4. **A reason and a reset time beside the status** (2026-10-20, renamed 2026-10-21): `metadata.reason`, a short text such as "rate limit" or "permission for npm test", and `resetsAt`, a time used only while paused, so the UI can count down and the server knows when to resume. On the CLI route `resetsAt` comes from the reset time Claude Code passes to a status-line command (`rate_limits.*.resets_at`, for the window at its limit), since the time on screen has no date and is not parsed; not every session gets one ([research](../../docs/research/0002-harness-bridge.md#usage-limits)), so `resetsAt` can stay empty. OpenCode's retry message and next time, Claude Code's `waitingFor` and Cloudflare's interrupted reason do the same.
5. **An optional task kind on the session** (2026-10-20), `metadata.task`, one of the thirteen on `/docs/ui/icons`, set by whoever starts the session, usually an orchestrator starting a subagent (`zerosdk session start --agent <id> --task debug`), since the glossary defines a subagent as started for one task, so the same agent can build one day and debug the next. No source has such a field; it is ZeroSDK's own, and a session started without one shows its status icon.
6. **A session names its agent by its `id`** (2026-10-20), `agentId`, the agent's UUID, which is also Claude's name for it, so renaming an agent never breaks its sessions; the UI shows the name by looking the `id` up. Seven of the nine sources reference by name; OpenCode references by id.
7. **A session keeps its parent, not its root** (2026-10-20, root dropped 2026-10-21). The server writes `parentId`, the session that asked for it, when it starts the session; the top of its tree, which the permission flipper needs, and its depth are both worked out from that short chain and are not stored.
8. **Title, issue and pull request are labels in `metadata`** (2026-10-20, reshaped 2026-10-21): `issue` (its `key`, such as `ZS-12`, and its `url`, set at start), `pr` (its `number` and `url`, filled in once the agent opens one), `branch` and `title` (set at start, renamable), all optional; the row composes `ZS-12#45 Add tools` and can link the issue and the pull request, as Claude Code's agent view shows a pull request label beside a session's name.
9. **The rest of the shape** (2026-10-21), field by field by the sources' consensus, is in [ADR 0010](../../docs/adr/0010-a-session-keeps-what-most-sources-keep.md): `id`, `cwd`, `status` and `updatedAt` are required, `prompt` is optional, and a start time, depth, root, model and a thread are left out.

## Steps

1. Done: add `packages/schema/src/session.ts` on the conventions `Agent` follows (Zod 4, fields grouped under `// required`, `// optional` and `// metadata` and A to Z within each, `id` as a UUID version 7, as `Agent`'s, a JSDoc description per field drafted from the sources' own wording), show it to the user before anything uses it, and record its shape in an ADR. Add a Session reference page after Agent, showing the type a session is written as and the sources' session types, each printed by a script, as `bun run schema:types` and `bun run schema:sources` do.
2. Done: key the icons by the schema's values, the way `effortIcons` is keyed by `Agent["effort"]`, as `statusIcons` (renamed from `stateIcons`) and `taskIcons`, and rename the icons page's State section to Status.
3. Done: make each sidebar row an `Agent` and its `Session`, build the nesting from the parent field, and fold `AgentRow`, `SubagentRow` and `NestedSubagentRow` into one row type, `SessionRow`.
4. Settle the [icebox: the sign-in session table](0002-auth-session-name.md) when the sessions table is designed, since agent sessions then get a table beside the sign-in `session` table.
5. Done: update the tests under `tests/web/next/src/components/agents/`, the `/docs/ui/sidebar` page and the `codebase-map` and `design` skills, and check the sidebar in a real browser.
